what_it_is.value: Open-source personal AI assistant that runs on your own machine and is used from chat apps such as WhatsApp and Telegram; it can manage inbox and calendar, browse, fill forms, read and write files and run shell commands.

runs_where.value: Your computer or your own server ('laptop, homelab, or VPS'). The homepage says 'No subscription. No hosted tier.' Third parties sell managed hosting (see openclaw-hosting).

platforms.value: Desktop apps for macOS 15+ (v2026.11.3), Windows 10/11 x64/ARM64 (v2026.11.1, marked Beta), Linux AppImage/.deb (v2026.11.2). Chat channels: WhatsApp, Telegram, Discord, Slack, Signal, iMessage and more, '29 channels' in total, DMs and group chats. Native iOS and Android apps paired to your own Gateway per a TechCrunch article (2026-06-30) featured on the homepage.
platforms.note: Mobile app claim is from the homepage's press section quoting TechCrunch; the TechCrunch article itself was not opened.

setup.value: Docs say 'Install OpenClaw, run onboarding, and chat with your AI assistant in about 5 minutes.' Main paths use a terminal (curl install script, npm i -g openclaw, or npx openclaw@latest) and need Node.js 24/26; desktop apps 'install everything for you'. Windows: native Windows Hub app is 'the easiest desktop path'. No Docker required for the default path.

ai_models.value: Bring your own: hosted, subscription-backed, gateway, or local models. Onboarding reuses an existing Claude Code or Codex CLI login or a provider API key. OAuth ('subscription auth') supported for OpenAI Codex (ChatGPT OAuth) and Anthropic Claude CLI reuse; docs say Anthropic staff told them CLI reuse 'is allowed again' but recommend API keys for Anthropic in production. Users pay their model provider; OpenClaw itself charges nothing.
ai_models.note: Anthropic subscription policy toward third-party harnesses changed during 2026 (see 03-keywords-competitors.md section 7); the OpenClaw doc is OpenClaw's own reading, not an Anthropic notice.

pricing.value: Free and open source (MIT). 'No subscription. No hosted tier. No token.' Model usage is paid to whichever provider you connect.

scheduling.value: Yes. Built-in scheduler ('Automations', CLI `openclaw automations`, alias `openclaw cron`) with one-shot and recurring jobs, webhooks and Gmail PubSub triggers, output delivered to a chat channel or webhook.

integrations.value: 29 chat channels per homepage; integrations listed include Claude, GPT, Gmail, GitHub, Obsidian, Twitter, Spotify, Hue, browser; skills and plugins via ClawHub.
integrations.note: No single claimed total integration count found.

multi_agent.value: Yes. Multiple isolated agents in one Gateway, each with its own workspace, auth and sessions, routed by 'bindings'; sub-agents; 'OpenClaw Multiplayer' (blog 2026-11-05) lets a team share one gateway. Works in group chats.

open_source.value: MIT license (Copyright 2026 OpenClaw Foundation). Repo github.com/openclaw/openclaw, 394,365 stars on 2026-11-12 via GitHub API; repo created 2025-11-24.

security.value: GitHub lists 722 published security advisories for the repo (14 critical, 249 high, 390 medium, 69 low) as of 2026-11-12, first published 2026-01-31 (e.g. '1-Click RCE via Authentication Token Exfiltration From gatewayUrl', GHSA-g8p2-7wf7-98mq) and many critical gateway privilege-escalation and sandbox-escape advisories in Feb to Apr 2026. Separately, Koi Security's audit of 2,857 ClawHub skills found 341 malicious ones (reported by The Hacker News, 2026-02-02). OpenClaw has since partnered with VirusTotal and NVIDIA for skill scanning and completed a Trail of Bits audit via OpenAI's 'Patch the Planet' initiative (per its blog).
security.note: Advisory counts from `gh api repos/openclaw/openclaw/security-advisories?state=published`. ClawHub malware source (secondary): https://thehackernews.com/2026/02/researchers-find-341-malicious-clawhub.html . Koi's own post did not render. Release reliability: OpenClaw apologised for broken 2026.4.24 to 2026.4.29 releases (https://openclaw.ai/blog/openclaw-rough-week, 2026-05-05).

status.value: Naming: 'Clawd' (Nov 2025, renamed after Anthropic's legal team asked), then 'Moltbot', then 'OpenClaw' announced 2026-01-29 (the repo's Docker advisory still says 'Clawdbot'). Creator Peter Steinberger announced on 2026-02-14 he is joining OpenAI and that OpenClaw 'will move to a foundation and stay open and independent'. The OpenClaw Foundation, a US 501(c)(3), was announced 2026-07-08 with a full-time staff; it says OpenAI has committed to keep the project open and independent.
status.note: Naming history: https://openclaw.ai/blog/introducing-openclaw (2026-01-29). OpenAI move: https://steipete.me/posts/2026/openclaw (2026-02-14); Help Net Security reported it 2026-02-16 (https://www.helpnetsecurity.com/2026/02/16/openclaw-creator-peter-steinberger-joins-openai/). 'Clawdbot' spelling is from advisory GHSA-mc68-q9jw-2h3v.

what_it_is.value: Open-source AI agent from Nous Research with persistent memory and self-created skills, reachable from a desktop app, terminal or messaging apps.

runs_where.value: Your computer or your server (README: 'Run it on a $5 VPS, a GPU cluster, or serverless infrastructure'); optional hosted cloud agent through Nous Portal on paid tiers.

platforms.value: Desktop app for macOS 12+ and Windows 10/11 (Microsoft Store or .exe); Linux via terminal install; Android via Termux package. Chat: Telegram, Discord, Slack, WhatsApp, Signal, Email, CLI.
platforms.note: Termux detail from the GitHub README. No iOS app found.

setup.value: Desktop app download, or a terminal one-liner (curl install script on macOS/Linux/WSL2, PowerShell on Windows). README quickstart says 'Install, setup, first conversation in 2 minutes'. You must connect a model provider.

ai_models.value: Any provider: Nous Portal (OAuth subscription), OpenRouter, OpenAI, own endpoints, Ollama/vLLM. Subscription sign-in: ChatGPT/Codex via ChatGPT OAuth; Anthropic OAuth only on a Claude Max plan and it bills only purchased extra usage, never the base Max allowance; Claude Pro cannot use it. API keys also supported.

pricing.value: Software free (MIT). Nous Portal plans: Free $0 pay-as-you-go (free models only); Plus $20/month; Super $100/month (5x Plus usage); Ultra $200/month (10x Plus). Paid tiers include 200+ models, hosted tools and one cloud agent (Plus 4 GB RAM/25 GB disk, Super 4 GB/100 GB, Ultra 8 GB/100 GB).

scheduling.value: Yes. Built-in cron scheduler with natural-language scheduling; delivers to any platform; runs unattended through the gateway.

integrations.value: README cites '40+ tools'; messaging platforms listed above; MCP compatible per docs index.

multi_agent.value: Yes. Isolated subagents for parallel workstreams, each with own conversation and terminal; configurable provider and model per subagent in Desktop.

open_source.value: MIT license. github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent, 262,734 stars on 2026-11-12 via GitHub API; repo created 2025-07-22.

security.value: No published GitHub security advisories returned by the GitHub API for the repo on 2026-11-12. Docs list command approval, DM pairing and container isolation; five sandbox backends (local, Docker, SSH, Singularity, Modal).
security.note: Absence of advisories is not evidence of absence of vulnerabilities.

status.value: Active; maintained by Nous Research. Hostinger sells a 'Managed Hermes Agent' alongside managed OpenClaw.

what_it_is.value: General-purpose AI agent that runs tasks in its own cloud computers to produce research, websites, slides, images and video.

runs_where.value: Their cloud (the Meta announcement post cites 'over 80 Million virtual computers'). A 'My Browser' product and desktop app also exist.
runs_where.note: How much runs locally in the desktop app was not verified.

platforms.value: Web; desktop apps for macOS and Windows; mobile apps for iOS and Android; Slack integration; messaging 'Manus Agents' in Telegram (launched 2026-02-16, all tiers) and WhatsApp Business (Business accounts only, per help center).
platforms.note: Download list from footer of manus.im pages; WhatsApp Business limit from help.manus.im search result (the article page did not load for me), so medium for WhatsApp.

setup.value: No install needed for web. Telegram: 'scan a QR code, and link Telegram in about a minute. No command lines, configuration files, or API tokens required.'

ai_models.value: Manus's own agent models (pricing lists Manus 2.0 Lite on Free, Manus 2.0 and 2.0 Max on Pro), paid with Manus credits. Pro adds 'Manus Flex: bring your own keys'.

pricing.value: Free $0 (300 credits/day, Manus 2.0 Lite, 3 tasks at once, 2 automations); Pro $20/month (4,000 credits/month, 20 tasks at once, 20 automations); Max $200/month (40,000 credits/month, pay as you go after credits). Annual billing saves 17%. Team and Enterprise plans separate.
pricing.note: Read from a rendered screenshot of the pricing page (monthly toggle). Credit dropdowns suggest higher credit options exist.

scheduling.value: Yes. Plans include a number of 'automations' (2 on Free, 20 on Pro); the Telegram launch post describes setting up a recurring task that delivers scheduled summaries in chat.

integrations.note: Manus has a /connectors section (78 pages in its sitemap) but I found no claimed total count.

multi_agent.value: Partly: 'Wide Research' across hundreds of sources and the chat agent 'can orchestrate sub-tasks behind the scenes'. No user-facing team of separate agents found.

open_source.note: No public repo found; inferred from product being a closed SaaS.

security.note: Nothing notable checked. Separation from Meta involved user data backup and deletion notices (see status).

status.value: Meta acquisition announced 2025-12-29 (Manus blog). China's NDRC ordered the deal unwound in April 2026; Manus said on 2026-09-01 it 'has formally resumed independent operations' with its founding team leading. During separation (notice 2026-08-11) some users had to back up data, and some user data may be lost.
status.note: Primary for the acquisition: https://manus.im/blog/manus-joins-meta-for-next-era-of-innovation (still live, dated Monday, December 29). Independence and unwind are from press: Global Times (2026-09-01) and Silicon Republic (https://www.siliconrepublic.com/business/manus-splits-from-meta-after-china-orders-reversal-of-2bn-deal). I did not open Manus's own independence announcement. Silicon Republic reports Tencent is set to become the largest external shareholder (reported, not confirmed).

what_it_is.value: Anthropic's agent mode for Claude that works across your chosen folders, apps and connectors to finish multi-step tasks and hand back finished work for review.

runs_where.value: Both: the desktop app works in folders and apps on your computer; tasks started from the phone 'keep working in the cloud even when your laptop is closed'.

platforms.value: Desktop (macOS, Windows; Linux desktop in beta for Ubuntu/Debian with Cowork available), web, iOS and Android. Slack connector included on Team plans.
platforms.note: Cowork page says it runs on desktop, web and mobile; Linux detail from the download page FAQ.

setup.value: No terminal. 'Download the desktop app and hand off your first task in minutes.' Requires a paid Claude plan.

ai_models.value: Anthropic Claude models only, included in your Claude subscription usage (Max mentions 'Fable included, up to half your weekly limit'). Enterprise can use Claude through their own cloud provider.
ai_models.note: Exact model list per plan not captured.

pricing.value: Free $0 (no hand off/schedule tasks); Pro $20/month monthly or $17/month annual ($200 up front); Max $100/month (5x Pro usage); Ultra $200/month; Team $20/seat/month annual or $25 monthly (Cowork included on standard and premium seats). Cowork works with a paid plan.

scheduling.value: Yes. 'Schedule a task for any cadence, and it runs unattended'; daily, weekly or monthly recurring reports. Pricing table lists 'Hand off and schedule tasks' on Pro, Max, Ultra (not Free).

integrations.value: Connectors and plugins (plugins bundle skills, connectors and sub-agents); built-in browser; computer use as a last resort.
integrations.note: No total connector count captured from opened pages.

multi_agent.value: Partly: big projects 'are split into chunks that run together'; plugins can include sub-agents. No user-facing group chat of agents.

security.value: You choose folders and tools; deleting anything needs approval; permission settings make Claude show its plan and wait; enterprise admins get spend limits and OpenTelemetry to SIEM.

status.value: Banner on 2026-11-12: 'Claude Cowork is now just Claude. Rolling out to Pro, Max, and Ultra, with more plans to follow.' Cowork capabilities are folded into Claude automatically when a task needs files.

pricing.value: Free $0/month (no credit card); Pro $19/month; Ultra $199/month (adds pay-as-you-go usage beyond credits). Monthly and yearly toggle.

scheduling.value: Yes: reminders, 'Handles tasks according to your schedule', and 'Real-time automations running in the background' on Pro.

integrations.value: Notion, GitHub, Linear 'and more' via a recipe directory; custom integrations via MCP. No total count claimed.

status.note: Deal value not in Cognition's post; TechCrunch reported 'low nine figures' (not opened).

what_it_is.value: 'Your team of always-on agents.' You create several named 'Bots'. They share a persistent cloud computer (browser, terminal, filesystem) and work across apps, websites and tools. Chat is the main interface, and voice calls and voice notes are also supported.

maker.value: Published by SpaceXSI (footer: SpaceX Super Intelligence LLC, formerly xAI) and built on Cursor infrastructure. Grok Bot signs in with a Cursor account, and its usage, billing, retention and deletion follow Cursor terms. Press calls it a SpaceXAI + Cursor launch.

launched.value: Launched in beta on Aug 11, 2026. At launch it was for SuperGrok/Plus/Heavy, Cursor Pro/Pro+/Ultra and Cursor Teams Standard/Premium subscribers, on desktop and iOS. Enterprise customers got a waitlist.

runs_where.value: In the cloud. Each user gets one persistent, dedicated, hardware-isolated cloud computer that all of their Bots share (files, browser sessions, logins). Bots are not a security boundary from each other.

works_when_off.value: Yes. 'Bot work runs on the cloud computer. Closing the app, laptop, or phone does not stop a background turn or routine.'

own_computer.value: Bots run commands on your own desktop only if you allow it under Settings > Computer > 'Execution on this computer', which by default asks every time. An optional 'Route traffic through this computer' setting makes sites see your home connection.

platforms.value: macOS (Apple silicon and Intel), Windows (x64 and Arm64), Linux (x64 and Arm64 as .deb, .rpm or AppImage), iPhone (iOS 18+, also iPad) and Android 9+. Bots can also be reached in X Chat, by tagging @bot on X, in Slack (Team Bots) and in Microsoft Teams. There is no general web chat app; the web has the dashboard and the marketplace.

setup.value: Download the app and sign in with a Cursor account; it needs a paid plan that includes Grok Bot (or a one-time trial credit on some accounts).
setup.note: combined from the faq (cursor sign-in, trial) and the pricing page

ai_models.value: Grok Bot picks the model and there is no model picker. A task may run on a first-party SpaceXSI (Grok) model or on a third-party model from a provider on Cursor's sub-processor list (the docs mention Opus 5.5). The model used is not shown to the user, and you cannot bring your own model or API key.

pricing.value: On The X Subscription, Grok Bot is included in Premium ($30/mo or $300/yr), Super ($100/mo) and Ultra ($200/mo). It is NOT included in Free or Plus ($8/mo). Team seats cost $30/$100/$200. There is no separate Grok Bot subscription.

pricing_legacy.value: On legacy plans, Grok Bot is included with every paid Cursor individual plan (Pro, Pro+, Ultra) and self-serve Teams. Users can instead link an individual SuperGrok, SuperGrok Plus, SuperGrok Heavy or X Premium+ subscription, or use a seat on a self-serve Grok Business plan. SuperGrok Lite and Grok Enterprise cannot link. Linking is permanent, and the two plans do not add together.

usage_limits.value: There is a weekly usage pool, shared with Grok and Cursor on The X Subscription. It is metered by agent steps and tokens, not by message count. Usage past the pool draws on prepaid credits (X Subscription) or on-demand billing (legacy Cursor). Super gets 15x and Ultra 50x the Plus base, versus 4x on Premium. No absolute numbers are published. Routines must be at least 5 minutes apart.

trial.value: Some accounts get a 'Start Trial' option: a one-time usage credit that also expires after 7 days. It never converts to a paid plan. Separately, an App Store trial in the iOS app does convert to a paid Apple subscription.

scheduling.value: A skill is a reusable set of instructions, invoked with '/'. A routine assigns a workflow to one Bot on a schedule (plain-language, time-zone aware, at least 5 minutes apart) or on an event: Slack message, GitHub/Linear/Sentry/PagerDuty event, email, or webhook. 'Teach a task' records a browser demonstration of up to 10 minutes and turns it into a skill (gradual rollout).

computer_use.value: Yes. Bots operate a browser and desktop on the cloud computer, and you can watch or take control. Each Bot gets its own screen, with one computer-use task per Bot at a time. CAPTCHAs, SSO, passkeys and similar steps are handed back to you. Logins come from Vault, 1Password or Secure Forms without the model seeing passwords. Some sites block cloud IPs.

memory.value: Each Bot keeps its own memory (preferences, rules, facts, a dated work log). A few facts, such as your name and time zone, are shared across Bots. Bots decide on their own what to save. There is no memory screen: to view or edit memory you ask the Bot in chat. 'Import Memory' can bring context over from another assistant.

integrations.value: Connectors include Gmail, Google Calendar, Google Drive, Slack, Notion, Microsoft Teams, Granola, OneDrive/SharePoint and 1Password, among others, via the Cursor marketplace. Custom MCP servers and APIs are supported. Other features: Bots joining meetings, Bot email addresses, and payment wallets (Link, X Money, Shop Pay).

multi_agent.value: Yes. Users run many Bots in parallel, typically with a 'primary Bot' that reports on the others. Bots can message each other, hand off work, and coordinate in group chats. Team Bots can be shared with coworkers.

privacy.value: Grok Bot uses Cursor authentication and data settings. It requires cloud data storage, so Cursor's Legacy Privacy Mode is not supported. Training opt-out follows Cursor privacy settings. Data can go to any provider on Cursor's sub-processor list, and team model allowlists do not apply to Grok Bot. Backend retention follows Cursor terms.

deletion.value: Grok Bot cannot be deleted without deleting your whole Cursor account. Deletion removes Bots, chats, computers and connected apps, and data is purged within 30 days.

export.value: I found no documented export for Bot conversations, memory or Bots as files. The docs only offer: per-file Download/Download all, exporting a call transcript or recording, and 'Share > Create a copy', which publishes a Bot template (identity, skills, routines, but no history or memory) as a link. Import exists only for memory (a paste-in prompt), Vault logins, and Bot templates. Deleting a Bot is irreversible.

open_source.value: No. A closed product from SpaceXSI built on Cursor.

complaints_cost.value: On Nov 1, 2026, Elon Musk posted: 'The cost of serving Grok Bot was unsustainably high relative to revenue', after users reported weekly allowances draining quickly. Many outlets covered it (TechRepublic, IBTimes, etc.).

complaints_allowance.value: A Cursor forum thread (Sep 10, 2026) reports a $200 Ultra plan hitting 99% of the weekly allowance in 3 days. Staff replied that billing counts tool and browser use, subagents and re-reading long conversations, and advised starting fresh conversations. In another thread (Aug 2026) a Pro+ user hit 77% in 2 days.

complaints_spill.value: A Cursor forum bug report (Aug 27, 2026) says Grok Bot moves into paid on-demand usage with no warning. Cursor staff said this was 'working as intended right now' and logged a feature request.

complaints_models.value: A Cursor forum thread (Oct 14, 2026) says Grok Bot 'now uses a variety of vendor's models, instead of just Grok' and that quality dropped. Other users agreed.

status.value: Live; beta label since launch on 11 August 2026. Usage limits were cut in early November 2026 after Musk said serving costs were unsustainably high.
